thread:
rebecca: Heads-up — BlueHarbor POC blocked. Dedicated GPU pool in ap-northeast1 never transitions to active. Getting NoAvailableCapacity + 429s from allocation service. Need swarming help ASAP.

miguel: @rebecca can you paste the pool id and the raw log snippet? also which reservation was requested (commit vs hourly burst)?

rebecca: Pool id: pool-6a2f
Error snippet:
```
2026-03-21T09:12:03Z ERROR allocation: NoAvailableCapacity region=ap-northeast1 requested_gpus=4 pool=pool-6a2f
2026-03-21T09:12:09Z WARN quota: reservation mismatch project=blueharbor-poc expected_label=reserved-commit-100 found_label=none
2026-03-21T09:12:09Z ERROR http: 429 allocation_service "rate limit" details="quota check failed"
```

miguel: hmmm reservation mismatch looks like the usual label/region mixup. run this to inspect reservation binding:
```
rictl reservations describe --project=blueharbor-poc --reservation-id=reserved-commit-100
```
If that shows us-west1, that's why allocation in ap-northeast1 fails.

sophie: I pulled the infra state — reservation reserved-commit-100 is bound to us-west1. BlueHarbor asked for APAC but sales accidentally selected the us-west SKU in the PO. I can create a new reservation in ap-northeast1, but we need approval from @alex for pricing commit.

alex: Short answer: creating a new committed reservation in APAC will bill pro-rata for the month. For a 2-week POC I recommend either: (1) create an hourly burst pool (no commit) or (2) create a short-term commit and offset with credit. I can quote both. Ping me the expected GPU-hours. :money_with_wings:

rebecca: Customer timeline is tight — wants test runs today. They also handed a security questionnaire that requires KMS-managed keys and audit-log retention for the Dedicated instance. Who owns the sec answers?

sophie: Security ques: we support KMS + audit logs for Private; for Dedicated within our tenant we can enable KMSEnable flag and forward logs to their SIEM via syslog. I can draft the answers but need a quick confirmation on the KMS provider (GCP KMS or external HSM).

raj: For immediate unblock, two options:
- Quick: fallback route to hosted (eu-west) for the POC runs, adjust routing policy in Console -> Model Routing -> add fallback region eu-west. This avoids provisioning delay.
- Permanent: create reservation in ap-northeast1, then rebind pool. When you see 429s, add exponential backoff (start 500ms -> 2s) and reduce concurrency so we don't flood allocation service.

miguel: We should also check quota at cloud provider level. Sometimes provider quota is exhausted even if our reservation exists. run `gcloud compute reservations describe` / cloud console check.

rebecca: Customer says they prefer APAC for latency. Sophie — can you spin a temporary hourly burst pool in ap-northeast1 while Alex confirms pricing for a short commit? If so I'll tell customer.

ops-bot: Incident created: INC-9832 — "BlueHarbor POC: Dedicated pool provisioning failed (ap-northeast1)" — assigned to eng-platform.

sophie: On it. Spinning hourly-burst pool now (sizing 4x A100). Will attach KMS policy stub for the security team. ETA ~28m. I'll post logs when ready.

alex: I'll DM @rebecca the two pricing options and a quick pro-rata calc.

rebecca: Thanks all. If the hourly pool passes we can proceed and then upgrade to committed reserve if customer signs. Will also share the sec questionnaire answers once Sophie posts the stub. :pray:

sophie: Update 28m: burst pool created: pool-6a2f-burst, status=active. Ran a quick smoke test, allocations succeeded. Posting smoke logs:
```
2026-03-21T09:41:12Z INFO allocation: allocated 4 gpus pool=pool-6a2f-burst region=ap-northeast1 run_id=smoke-1
2026-03-21T09:41:13Z INFO runtime: start container image=redwood/runtime:1.8 commit=abc123
```

rebecca: Perfect. I'll update the customer and pause the committed reservation creation until Alex confirms. Closing the swarming for now, will re-open if anything else pops up. :white_check_mark:
